notes.meaning: An honest person living in poverty has far more honor than a wealthy fool who twists the truth. Integrity matters much more to God than money or high social standing. True happiness comes from an upright life rather than dishonest gain.
Eagerness without understanding often leads to serious trouble. Rushing ahead into decisions without knowing God's will makes a person lose their footing and miss the right path.

People often ruin their own lives through foolish choices. Then, instead of admitting their own mistakes, they get angry and blame the Lord for their troubles. Taking responsibility for our actions protects us from bitter feelings toward God.

Riches easily attract a crowd of fair-weather companions who only want personal gain. A poor person, on the other hand, is quickly deserted when their resources run out. Selfish people value money far more than genuine friendship.
Anyone who lies in court or spreads false stories will face certain justice. Even if human judges fail to catch them, God knows the truth and will not let them escape punishment.
Crowds of people line up to flatter powerful leaders and generous givers. Many will pretend to be friends just to receive gifts and favors.

When someone becomes poor, even their own family members often avoid them. Former friends keep their distance, and pleading for help brings no answer. Poverty quickly reveals who truly cares and who does not.
Seeking wisdom shows genuine care for your own life and future. Treasuring good understanding brings lasting success and blessing.
God takes false testimony very seriously and will not overlook it. People who build their lives on deceit and lies will eventually be ruined by them.
A fool does not have the character or wisdom to handle luxury and ease. It is even more unfitting when an untrained servant is elevated to rule harshly over leaders.
Good understanding helps a person pause and stay calm instead of reacting in anger. Choosing to overlook an insult or minor offense brings real honor rather than weakness.
A king's anger strikes terror like a roaring lion hunting its prey. His favor brings life and refreshment, like morning dew helping parched grass grow.
A rebellious child brings continuous grief and ruin to a father's household. In the same way, constant arguing from a spouse wears down a home like water dripping endlessly through a leaky roof.
Parents can pass down family homes and wealth to their children. A wise, sensible wife, however, is a special gift that comes straight from the Lord.
Laziness numbs the mind and makes an idle person act as if they are in a deep sleep. Refusing to work will inevitably leave someone with an empty stomach.
Obeying God's commandments protects a person's life and soul. Living carelessly without caring whether your actions please God leads straight to ruin and death.
Helping the poor is treated by God as lending directly to Him. The Lord notices every act of mercy and promises to repay the giver with His own blessing.
Parents need to correct their children early while their hearts can still be shaped for good. Holding back proper discipline out of soft pity leaves a child on a dangerous path toward destruction.
A person with an uncontrolled temper will repeatedly face painful consequences. Bailing them out of trouble will not cure the underlying problem, and you will soon have to rescue them again.
Listening to wise advice and accepting correction prepares a person for the future. Learning humility when you are young ensures that your later years will be full of wisdom.
People make countless plans and schemes about what they want to accomplish. In the end, only the purpose of the Lord will stand and prevail over human designs.
What people truly desire and value in others is faithful kindness. A poor person who desires to help is far better than a wealthy liar who makes empty promises.
Living with reverent respect toward the Lord leads to genuine life. It brings quiet contentment and shields a person from harmful evil.
A lazy person will dip a hand into the food bowl but feel too tired to bring it back to their mouth. This humorous picture shows how ridiculous and helpless extreme laziness can make someone.

Punishing an arrogant mocker may not change his heart, but it teaches simple and impressionable people to steer clear of evil. A wise person, by contrast, needs only a gentle rebuke to learn and grow.
A son who mistreats his father or drives away his own mother is a terrible disgrace. Harming one's parents brings lasting shame and violates God's law.
Turning away from sound instruction puts a person on a fast track toward error. If you stop listening to wise teaching, you will quickly wander from what is right.
A dishonest witness mocks the very idea of fair justice in court. Wicked people swallow down evil and wrongdoing as eagerly as if it were delicious food.
Severe punishment is already prepared for those who mock what is holy. Those who choose foolish rebellion will certainly receive the painful discipline they deserve.
